ledger.x: 20: Vannius becomes client king of the Quadi.
20: the Marcomanni exiles live under Vannius.
20: the Quadi kingdom of Vannius is a client of Rome.
50/51: Vangio and Sido divide the realm.
173: the Quadi expel their Roman-approved king and the client relation ends.

180: peace. By 180 there were 'Roman garrisons of 20,000 men each permanently stationed in both countries' (the Marcomanni and the Quadi) and Marcus Aurelius 'died in 180 while considering a province called Marcomannia'; 'Commodus negotiated peace with the Marcomanni and Quadi'. The rebellion…
about 409: the Quadi leave their homeland.

wars.name: Marcomannic Wars
wars.outcome: Roman victory, status quo ante bellum: the Quadi left the coalition in 171, rebelled in 173 and again in 177, accepted Roman garrisons in 174, and were beaten at Laugaricio (179); Commodus made peace in 180.

wars.name: Campaigns of Carinus and Numerian against the Quadi
wars.outcome: 'Carinus and Numerian held campaigns against the Quadi in 283-284'; the Quadi were 'again listed among attackers in 285'.

wars.name: Constantius II's Danube campaign against the Quadi
wars.outcome: Constantius II crossed the Danube; Vitrodorus, son of King Viduarius (probably of the western Quadi), swore loyalty to Rome.

wars.name: Quadi and Sarmatian invasion of Illyricum
wars.outcome: A Roman general murdered King Gabinius at dinner in 374 over a fort; 'the Quadi, who had long been quiet, were suddenly aroused to an outbreak'; the Germanic Wars page has the Quadi and Sarmatians invading former Illyricum in 374.

certainty.note: The pages give homeland river names, not boundaries.
